text:
maria: heads-up — saw ~28 GPU nodes in us-west1-g go NotReady/NoSchedule right after the node-image rollout at 03:10UTC
kevin: :eyes: any obvious kubelet errors?
maria: kubelet saying 'Failed to start device plugin' and device-plugin DaemonSet CrashLoopBackOff on those nodes
jasmin: k8s-event-bot posted a bunch of events: Node/ip-10-2-7-45 NotReady: Kubelet stopped posting node status
k8s-event-bot: Node ip-10-2-7-45 condition: Ready=False reason:KernelModuleError message: 'nvidia module failed to initialize'
maria: checked one node via SSH — dmesg shows 'nvidia: module verification failed: signature and taint' and NVML init errors
kevin: likely kernel vs driver mismatch. Which node-image did the rollout use?
maria: the 2026-03-18-rt-kernel tag (auto-rolled from nodepool). Previous image worked fine.
sam: cluster-autoscaler spun up 6 extra gpu instances trying to satisfy pending jobs but they never registered because device plugin never came up — so wasting $$ :facepalm:
jasmin: quick logs from device plugin on that node: `kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin -l k8s-app=nvidia-device-plugin --tail=200`
jasmin: error snippet: "failed to initialize NVML: unknown error (NVIDIA-SMI was unable to find GPU driver)"
kevin: that matches driver/kernel ABI mismatch. Did the node image include kernel-headers?
maria: not the right headers. Also noticed the daemonset image is v0.10.0 — we upgraded it last month but nodes expect v0.12.0 (with new init flow)
kevin: two separate issues then: kernel+driver mismatch in the new image and an older device-plugin that can't work around it. Oof.
jasmin: mitigation plan?
maria: immediate: cordon affected nodes, drain where safe. For the heavy inference pools we'll move jobs to dedicated fallback cluster (us-east1)
sam: creating a script to detect device-plugin Ready before marking node as healthy to avoid autoscaler mirroring the problem. If autoscaler sees node registered but pods not schedulable it still thinks capacity exists. We should block that.
kevin: short-term rollback: revert node-image for the GPU nodepool to previous stable AMI and trigger rolling replace (nodepool API) — @kevin will do this for us-west1-g canary group
kevin: command I'll run: `gcloud compute instances resize-instance-group-manager --version template=projects/...` (will do offline)
jasmin: and I'll bump the nvidia-device-plugin DaemonSet to v0.12.0 and add readinessProbe that checks NVML init, then rollout to one node first
maria: tests: on one canary node run `sudo dkms status` and `nvidia-smi` after reboot, expect GPUs visible.
kevin: also add a preflight in the nodepool rollout job: after instance comes up, check `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=nvidia-device-plugin -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.phase}'` and only mark node healthy when device-plugin is Running
sam: filing an infra ticket and a short postmortem. Cost hit estimate: ~6 wasted nodes for 2 hours -> ~US$1.2k (rough ballpark).
jasmin: FYI some pods are annotated with tolerations for gpu:NoSchedule and cluster-autoscaler is not aware of device-plugin health, so it won't scale down those failed nodes automatically
maria: temporary workaround: add taint to the affected nodepool so scheduler avoids scheduling new critical inference pods until we fix drivers
kevin: timeline: revert canary in next 20m, monitor. If green, schedule rolling revert for remaining nodes overnight.
jasmin: long-term: add automated compatibility test in node-image pipeline (boot node, install driver, run `nvidia-smi`) and add device-plugin readiness gating to autoscaler health checks
sam: assigning owners in ticket: kevin -> node-image rollback, jasmin -> device-plugin bump + readinessProbe, maria -> rollout coordination + cost estimate, sam -> autoscaler health gating prototype
infra-bot: Incident ticket INFRA-2026-042 created by maria: gpu-nodepool-notready-2026-03-18
maria: thanks everyone. keep updates here, ping me if you need to borrow capacity from us-east1
kevin: starting revert now, will post progress
jasmin: I'll push DS change to canary namespace and watch logs :party_parrot:
maria: update 03:34UTC — canary node came back Ready after rollback + DS bump. Device-plugin Running and nvidia-smi OK
sam: autoscaler prototype ran a canary check and prevented creating new gpu nodes for 12m while waiting for device-plugin -> saved ~2 instances already
kevin: rolling revert scheduled — will stagger to limit impact on jobs
jasmin: follow-up: draft of postmortem + checklist for future rollouts, will drop in #postmortems later
maria: closing thread for now, reopen if anything resurfaces :thumbsup:"
